name: The Topkapı Palace Courtyard Plane

location.address: Topkapı Sarayı, near Orta Kapu / the Second Courtyard, Cankurtaran, Fatih

access: Paid entry: this tree stands inside Topkapı Palace's ticketed grounds (past Orta Kapu), so a museum ticket is required to reach it
transport: 5-10 min walk from Gülhane or Sultanahmet tram stops (T1 line)
verify_notes: NOT the famous Yeniçeriler Çınarı (Janissaries' Plane) of Topkapı's FIRST courtyard that reportedly witnessed the 1453 conquest and died/dried out between 1900 and 1930 (confirmed dead via istanbulansiklopedisi.org and multiple news pieces; this is already reflected in the city file's own intro and must never be revived as a live entry). This is a DIFFERENT, still-standing specimen further inside the palace grounds. Source 1 is Turkiye's national monumental-tree registry (Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığı, anitagaclar.gov.tr / underlying ArcGIS feature service turkiye_anit_agaclari, OBJECTID 140), which records this individual Platanus orientalis at either 778 years (per the rendered HTML detail page) or 783 years (per a fresh direct query of the same underlying feature service the same day), likely a snapshot-date difference; presented here as a range rather than picking one figure. The registry's own free-text 'Ağaç Hikayesi' field for this record is boilerplate history of Topkapı Palace generally and mis-cites its source URL as a page about a Porsuk (yew), not a çınar, the same story/species content-pairing bug already documented for ist_001 elsewhere in this registry, so the narrative text itself is not trustworthy, only the structured fields (species, age, girth, coordinates, il/ilçe). The rendered HTML page also displays 'Bulunduğu İl/İlçe: İstanbul - GÖLBAŞI', which is contradictory (Gölbaşı is an Ankara district, not an Istanbul one); the underlying ArcGIS feature service itself correctly carries il_adi=İstanbul, ilce_adi=Fatih for this and all nearby records, so this looks like a front-end display bug rather than a geocoding error, but it is recorded here as a reason for caution. Source 2 corroborates existence and species only, not this exact age: Hürriyet's survey of Istanbul's centuries-old planes and other Turkish coverage describe officially protected monumental çınar trees standing today in Topkapı's first and second courtyards, especially around the Imperial Council (Divan-ı Hümayun) and Bab-ı Selam / Orta Kapu, consistent with this record's coordinates, but no independent source gives a specific number matching 778-783 for this individual tree. Because of the age uncertainty and the registry's own documented data-quality issues, this entry is flagged and location_precision is set to approximate (palace-courtyard level, not a confirmed exact trunk position); a future pass with eyes on the ground or a cleaner primary source should tighten both. Also worth noting for the fetch-blocklist: a related registry mirror domain, avrupaanitagaclar.com, which several nearby ArcGIS records cite as their detail-page URL, has been compromised/hijacked and as of this pass (2026-08-08) serves unrelated Vietnamese gambling content (a site calling itself '78win') instead of tree data; it should not be fetched or trusted as a source going forward.
